title: Jinhan
capsule: Jinhan was a loose confederacy of twelve chiefdoms (samhan) in the southeastern Korean peninsula, documented in the Chinese Sanguo zhi (third century CE) as occupying the region east of the Nakdong River. It developed alongside Mahan to its west and Byeonhan to its south from roughly the first century BCE, engaging in iron production and trade with the Han commanderies and the Wa of the Japanese archipelago. By the fourth century CE the confederation dissolved as the Saro chiefdom rose to dominance, evolving into the kingdom of Silla, which formally unified the region by 378.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is poorly defined; boundaries are reconstructed from Chinese dynastic accounts and archaeological distributions of pottery and iron artifacts, with no fixed political borders.
